column1: # D11-CEIL mutgate spec — the two constants 013 D11-CEIL moved.
# Each row breaks THE BEHAVIOUR ITS ROW NAMES and must turn that row red:
#     baseline GREEN -> mutated RED -> restored GREEN, bytes identical.
# ROW 1 DOES NOT REVERT TO 80000, AND THE REASON IS THE BEST SINGLE PIECE OF
# EVIDENCE FOR THIS WHOLE CHANGE. The brief asked for the ceiling to be reverted.
# Tried, twice: a cold run in the mutgate clone came in at 79000 ms against the
# reverted 80000 and PASSED BY ONE SECOND, scoring the row vacuous. The old
# ceiling sits INSIDE the noise band of current cold runs (79-111 s observed),
# so reverting to it is a coin toss and not a discriminator -- and that is
# precisely why CI passed once at exactly 80000 against 80000 and then failed at
# 106000. A gate whose pass depends on which second it lands in is the failure
# this re-measurement exists to end; it cannot also be the proof.
# So the mutation is 180000 -> 50000: WI-D4's own measured slow end, the
# ceiling's previous generation of measurement, and comfortably below every cold
# sample ever observed here. The row then discriminates deterministically, and
# what it proves is the thing that matters -- that `pr_target_ceiling_ms()` is
# load-bearing, read by the recipe, and fails the target when it is too low.
# ROW 1 MUST FORCE A COLD COMPILE, and getting this wrong scores the row
# VACUOUS when the mutation is in fact perfectly sound. `make corpus_pr` only
# exceeds any plausible ceiling COLD: 87-90 s cold against 31 s warm, measured
# in this clone. mutgate runs baseline, mutated and restored in the SAME repo,
# so runs 2 and 3 are warm unless something makes them cold, and a warm 31 s
# run passes the reverted 80000 ceiling exactly as happily as the real one.
# `rm -rf .ailang` DOES NOT DO IT, which is the trap worth recording. The
# AILANG compile cache is not in the tree: it is GLOBAL, at ~/.ailang/cache,
# and keyed such that a clone at a NEW PATH misses it — which is why a fresh
# clone is cold at all, and why the tree's own .ailang is 112K of corpus
# store and nothing else. Deleting it changes nothing. Nor may this spec wipe
# the global cache: it is shared with every other agent working in this
# container. So each run points AILANG_CACHE_DIR at its own empty temp dir --
# cold by construction, shared state untouched -- and removes it afterwards,
# because a cold run leaves 154M behind.
# ROW 2 IS NOT A REVERT, AND THE REASON IS WORTH READING BEFORE CHANGING IT.
# The brief asked for `measured_ms_per_seed()` to be REVERTED to 381. That
# mutation does not discriminate, and not because the test is weak: the
# constant moved UP (381 -> 416), so reverting it buys MORE seeds per budget
# (5000/381 = 13 against 5000/416 = 12) and the check it feeds --
# `seeds_affordable_in(budget) >= minimum_seeds` -- passes more comfortably
# than it does on the real code. A mutation that makes a test pass harder is
# not a test of anything. What the check NAMES is "the declared minimum fits
# the budget at the measured per-seed cost", so the mutation that breaks it is
# one where the cost no longer fits: 416 -> 417 gives 5000/417 = 11 < 12.
# That the mutation is ONE MILLISECOND is the finding, not a convenience. It is
# a direct demonstration that the margin under `pr_job()` is now exactly zero.
# NO PIPES IN A test_cmd: mutgate runs `eval` under `set -o pipefail`, so a
# `cmd | grep -q X` takes SIGPIPE and scores a BASELINE RED (exit 141) that
# says nothing about the row. Both rows redirect to a log and return the
# command's own exit status.
# fix_id
d11_ceiling
column3: s/^export pure func pr_target_ceiling_ms() -> int { 180000 }$/export pure func pr_target_ceiling_ms() -> int { 50000 }/
column4: d=$(mktemp -d); AILANG_CACHE_DIR=$d make corpus_pr > /tmp/d11_ceiling.log 2>&1; rc=$?; rm -rf $d; exit $rc

column1: d11_per_seed
column3: s/^export pure func measured_ms_per_seed() -> int { 416 }$/export pure func measured_ms_per_seed() -> int { 417 }/
